questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Right triangle ABC has the right angle at C, legs a = BC, b = AC, and hypotenuse c = AB. The altitude from C meets AB at D. Prove that a² + b² = c².
questions.prompt_markup: Right triangle ABC has the right angle at C, legs a = BC, b = AC, and hypotenuse c = AB. The altitude from C meets AB at D. Prove that a² + b² = c².
questions.required_method: Show △ACD ~ △ABC and △CBD ~ △ABC (AA), write two proportions, and add.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: △ADC ~ △ACB (shared ∠A, right angles), so AD/AC = AC/AB and b² = c · AD; △CDB ~ △ACB (shared ∠B), so BD/BC = BC/AB and a² = c · BD; adding, a² + b² = c(AD + BD) = c · c = c². Invalid: assuming a² + b² = c² anywhere; using the distance formula (it depends on the theorem).

questions.prompt: In right triangle ABC with the right angle at C, legs a and b, and hypotenuse c, the altitude from C meets AB at D. Similar triangles give b² = c · AD and a² = c · BD. Show how these give a² + b² = c².
questions.prompt_markup: In right triangle ABC with the right angle at C, legs a and b, and hypotenuse c, the altitude from C meets AB at D. Similar triangles give b² = c · AD and a² = c · BD. Show how these give a² + b² = c².
questions.correct_answer: a² + b² = c · BD + c · AD = c(BD + AD) = c · c = c², since AD + DB = AB = c.
questions.grading_note: Any correct algebra, including why AD + BD = c (D is between A and B).

branch.new_demand: See the theorem as the C = 90° case of a general relationship, and classify triangles by comparing squares.
branch.builds_on: A second extension of MAIN: FORWARD 1 extracts more right-triangle relationships; FORWARD 2 generalizes to all triangles (advanced strand).

questions.prompt: For a triangle with sides a, b, c and angle C opposite c, the Law of Cosines says c² = a² + b² - 2ab cos C. What does it become when C = 90°?
